blocks.title: A line you can see
blocks.content:
On a gravel descent, a rider watches the loose stones right in front of the wheel. Each stone prompts a small steering correction. Farther along, the road bends out of view. The rider has little time to decide where to slow down.

The useful change is to look far enough ahead to choose a line while still checking what is close. If the next part of the road is hidden, reduce speed before you reach it.

blocks.label: Look for the next usable line
blocks.content:
On a clear stretch, find a line that continues through the next few bike lengths. Let your gaze move between that line and the near surface when an obstacle needs attention. Keep your hands able to steer and brake.

You should be able to say where you plan to ride next. If you cannot, slow down until the line becomes visible.

Looking ahead gives you time to choose a line before you need to steer. Looking only at the front tire leaves each rock or rut as a last-second decision. Looking only at the exit can hide an obstacle between you and it.

Use a moving scan. Check the line ahead, glance nearer when the surface calls for it, then return to where you want the bike to go. How far ahead you look depends on speed, visibility, and the ground. A blind corner or loose patch calls for more room to slow down.

blocks.title: Look, scan, choose
blocks.description: Practice this on a familiar road with a clear sightline.

steps.detail: Ride at an easy pace where you can see your route through the next bend or obstacle.
Look for a clear path ahead rather than following the front wheel.
Glance toward the near surface when you need to confirm a rock, rut, or loose patch. Keep your eyes moving.
If the line disappears or the surface changes, slow down while you still have a predictable place to brake.

blocks.content: During a race, the road narrows and a bend hides the exit. Riders ahead may carry speed through it. Choose a pace based on what you can see, leave space, and look for your own line once the road opens.

blocks.title: Look, scan, choose
blocks.description: Repeat a short, low-traffic section at an easy pace. Notice whether you can name the line ahead and the nearest hazard without staring at either.

variants.label: Open, mostly flat gravel
steps: Pick a familiar section with a clear sightline and room to stop.
Before rolling, point to the line you plan to use.
Ride through slowly, moving your gaze between that line and the nearby surface as needed.
Stop and note whether you had time to adjust for a change in the ground. If not, choose an easier pace or section.

variants.label: A visible bend or surface change
steps: Choose a familiar bend with a clear exit and no traffic.
Approach at a pace that leaves room to brake before the bend.
Look through the bend, check the near surface as needed, and adjust your line before reaching the change.
Repeat only when you can explain your line and where you would slow down.

proof_gate.description: You can identify a visible line and a place to slow down before reaching a surface change.
proof_gate.target: Describe the line and your speed decision after an easy repeat; choose a slower route if the view is blocked.

blocks.content:
### When the scan breaks down

If you keep looking at one rock, lower your speed and give yourself more time to choose a path around it. If you stare at the far exit and miss the near surface, bring your gaze back briefly to check the ground. If a rider ahead blocks your view, add space instead of following their wheel into a line you cannot see.

blocks.question: You approach a gravel bend whose exit is hidden. What should guide your next move?

options.text: Match the speed of the rider ahead
Slow down where you can see and control the bike, then choose a line as the bend opens
Look only at the exit and ignore the near surface
Look at the front tire until the bend ends

blocks.explanation: Your pace should leave room to respond within the road you can see. Keep scanning between the intended line and nearby hazards.

blocks.content: On your next easy gravel ride, pick one visible bend. Note where you chose a line, what you checked near the wheel, and where you decided to slow down.
The next lesson covers braking. You will use the line you can see to choose where to reduce speed before a turn or a change in surface.
